claims.text: The initial Mg-containing lightweight HEA is a non-equilibrium, metastable solid solution with a homogeneous Mg distribution.
Service-relevant thermal aging activates Mg diffusion in the alloy.
Diffusing Mg segregates preferentially to defects and grain boundaries.
Mg segregation nucleates and promotes the growth of Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates.
The Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates occur primarily along grain boundaries and phase interfaces.
Thermal processing can transform an HEA solid solution into a multiphase state containing intermetallic phases.
Mg-rich intermetallic precipitation interrupts or destabilizes the protective oxide or passivation layer.
Aged samples will have a fragmented or less coherent protective oxide layer than the initial solid-solution state.
Intermetallic precipitation and oxide-layer disruption reduce high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the initial state.
Intermetallic precipitation and oxide or passivation-layer disruption reduce corrosion resistance relative to the initial state.
A homogeneous Mg distribution in the initial state supports a continuous protective oxide or passivation layer.
The initial homogeneous solid-solution state has higher corrosion and oxidation resistance than the aged precipitate-containing state.
Temperatures of approximately 800–1200 °C represent relevant service-regime limits for high-temperature oxidation testing of the proposed alloy.
Acidic or chloride-rich media are relevant corrosion environments for evaluating the proposed alloy.
Below the Mg-diffusion and precipitation regime, or at sufficiently short aging times, the alloy retains its homogeneous structure and protective behavior.
The temperature and time thresholds for significant Mg diffusion and intermetallic formation are not yet determined.

Failure to observe statistically significant Mg grain-boundary segregation or Mg-rich intermetallic formation, or finding equivalent oxidation and corrosion behavior in aged and initial samples, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
